events.label: founding
events.text: Newspaper founded as Päivälehti in Finland.

evidence.quote: The paper was founded in 1889 as Päivälehti

events.label: closure
events.text: Päivälehti closed permanently after Russian censorship pressure.
Proprietors reopened the paper under its current name.

evidence.quote: Its proprietors re-opened the paper under its current name in 1905

events.text: Paper became politically independent and non-aligned.

evidence.quote: has been politically independent and non-aligned since the 1932

events.text: Finnish and English-language online editions began.

evidence.quote: Between 1999 and 2012 there were also both Finnish and English-language online newspaper editions

events.text: English-language International Edition launched to inform readers about Finland.

evidence.quote: The International Edition launched on 14 September 1999

events.text: Finnish and English-language online editions ended.

evidence.quote: Between 1999 and 2012 there were also both Finnish and English-language online newspaper editions
The Helsingin Sanomat International Edition closed down on 26 October 2012

events.text: Paper switched from broadsheet to compact format.

evidence.quote: The newspaper was published in broadsheet format until 6 January 2013
Mikael Pentikäinen was the editor-in-chief until May 2013 when he was fired from the post

events.text: Riikka Venäläinen temporarily replaced him as editor-in-chief.

evidence.quote: until May 2013 when he was fired from the post
Riikka Venäläinen replaced him temporarily in the post
the service was discontinued on 6 October 2014

undated_mentions: Kaius Niemi became editor-in-chief after Riikka Venäläinen (no date given)
Eljas Erkko served as the paper's publisher during the run-up to the Winter War (no year stated)
Paper published some material in Russian for a while (no date given)
